mode: independent criterion scoring of isolated decision simulation
input_policy: Read only the simulation, four scenario input files, and four matching criteria files for substantive scoring. Did not read the current skill, research, previous scores, or proposed fixes. No delegation or source modifications.
scoring_policy: pass: actual decision/disclosure satisfies the atomic criterion under a reasonable interpretation; fail: absent required decision or contradicted criterion; not_assessable: supplied response cannot establish the decision. Planned checks count only as requirements in this no-live-actions simulation, never as completed execution. Negative criteria can pass from an explicit boundary decision without requiring claims of actual native enforcement.
limitations: This assesses simulated instructions and disclosures only. No live edit, test, merge, release, worker invocation, stop, ownership transfer, archive, or native enforcement was independently exercised.
Supplied passing evidence is accepted only as scenario context; its execution, accuracy, and runtime applicability outside the scenario were not reproduced.
The model route and reasoning effort are not exposed in the simulation metadata.
Some requirements are expressed at action level without exact commands. Those are acceptable for decision simulation when the relevant object, condition, and remaining gap are identifiable.
The shared-contract scope response does not claim native enforcement, so its negative criterion passes; it does not establish that assigned paths are enforced.

The task-context skill-loading requirement fails the hidden criterion even though most substantive task context is self-contained. Whether supplied accessible references would actually be available is not demonstrated.

gaps.summary: Requires loading the evaluated skill acceptance rules from unspecified accessible references, rather than making skill loading optional and the task sufficient on its own.

quote_verification.method: Every quoted string checked for exact substring membership in the associated response; criterion counts and case IDs checked against all four source pairs.
